title: Regular domain divisor quotient of canonical strict henselization
statement: Let R be regular, R/(f) regular, and b(f) nonunit at a geometric point. The divisor quotient of the canonical strict henselization is regular and a domain.

source.place: Tag 0EYG (pione-lemma-abhyankar-one-divisor), strict henselization paragraph; Tag 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization); Tag 06LN, regularity under strict henselization.

proof.text: Use smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso to compare the small and full affine-neighbourhood colimits. The final-functor coprojection formula and the structural-map equations identify the maps to the base. Compose b with the comparison and transport its nonunit hypothesis through the inverse. Apply the retained upstream regularity and domain components to this composite. Ideal.quotientEquiv for the inverse comparison identifies their full-colimit principal quotient with the original small-colimit principal quotient. Transport regularity using IsRegularRing.of_ringEquiv and the domain property using MulEquiv.isDomain_iff, and pair the results.

proof_origin.place: Tags 04HX, 05WS, 06LN and 00NP; retirement of the duplicate Sheaf domain component in favor of its proved upstream owner
proof_origin.note: The upstream theorem, all consumer signatures, and every mathematical dependency are preserved. The consumer now transports both properties through the same quotient equivalence.

theorem strictHenselizationRing_regular_divisor_quotient
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsRegularRing R] (f : R)
    [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})]
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (barY : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec R)
    (b : R ⟶ strictHenselizationRing barY)
    (hb : Spec.map b = strictHenselizationStructuralMap barY)
    (hg : ¬ IsUnit (b.hom f)) :
    IsRegularRing (strictHenselizationRing barY ⧸ Ideal.span {b.hom f}) ∧
      IsDomain (strictHenselizationRing barY ⧸ Ideal.span {b.hom f})
